name: Lieutenant's Insignia
summary: Within Durotar, Lieutenant's Insignia carries the Burning Blade's mark. Horde adventurers recover it from cultists near Orgrimmar.

sections.title: A Mark of the Cult
sections.body: Cultists at Skull Rock on Durotar's eastern shore carry Lieutenant's Insignia. The emblem marks its bearer as an officer of the Burning Blade. Warchief Thrall will not tolerate traitors in his new nation, but a purge could scatter the cult before its masters are exposed. He gives the badge to a trusted champion to test suspected infiltrators beneath Orgrimmar.

sections.title: The Cleft of Shadow
sections.body: Warchief Thrall sends his agent to the Cleft of Shadow with Lieutenant's Insignia, to present it to Neeru Fireblade. Neeru mistakes the agent for a newly promoted subordinate. Confident in his standing, the warlock boasts that the Burning Blade serves the Shadow Council and the Burning Legion. His words give Thrall a way to expose the corruption beneath the city.

faq.q: Where does the Lieutenant's Insignia come from?
aliases: how do i get lieutenants insignia
faq.answer: Burning Blade fanatics and apprentices in Skull Rock carry the Lieutenant's Insignia. The cavern lies on the coast east of Orgrimmar, in Durotar.

faq.q: What is the insignia used for?
aliases: why do i need lieutenants insignia
faq.answer: Warchief Thrall gives the insignia to his agent as a disguise. A young adventurer bearing it can pass as a Burning Blade officer and reach places Thrall's own agents cannot, to learn who leads the cult.
Neeru Fireblade is an orc warlock in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. He claims to serve Thrall by showing how warlocks can aid the Horde, but secretly leads the local Burning Blade cult.

faq.q: Why doesn't Thrall just kill Neeru Fireblade immediately?
faq.answer: Thrall knows Neeru is a traitor, but an early strike could warn the cult's true masters and scatter its network. He uses Neeru as an unwitting informant to uncover the Shadow Council's wider presence in Durotar.

angles.text: For the young Horde, the insignia marks the danger of demonic corruption trying to undermine Thrall's new nation from within.
For a warlock, the badge shows the Burning Blade turning fel magic to the Burning Legion's service, straining Thrall's tolerance of lawful Horde warlocks.
